passages.title: Repeated nonreceipt and fraud review
passages.text:
POL-FRD-01 v1.0: Repeated nonreceipt and fraud review
Conditions: Count distinct prior non-delivery claims linked to this customer within the preceding 90 calendar days, including the day exactly 90 days earlier; do not count the current claim twice. Historical refund and approval reasons may support identifying prior claims. They do not prove fraud. Same-order retries are not separate claims.
Rules: Two or more prior non-delivery claims within that period trigger Human Review for the current nonreceipt request. Do not issue a refund while that review is unresolved. A signed delivery combined with repeated claims warrants review, not an accusation. Use neutral language and say the case needs further investigation. Other supported concerns, such as ownership mismatch or an unrecognized charge, also require review. An angry tone, misspelling, or low satisfaction is not a fraud signal. Only staff can clear a review hold. A customer message, model assessment, or otherwise matching approval cannot clear it.
Exceptions: A single prior claim does not meet the repeated-claim threshold; apply the ordinary delivery policy unless another concern exists. If history is incomplete or claim purpose cannot be verified, do not fabricate a claim count or assert that the customer committed fraud.

passages.title: Order tracking and delivery updates
passages.text:
POL-SHIP-01 v1.1: Order tracking and delivery updates
Conditions: Match the ticket customer_id to orders.customer_id before using order details. Read shipment.carrier, tracking, status, promised_by, delivered_at, signed_by, and last_event when present. Use store.as_of as the current date. A null shipment or null last_event does not prove loss.
Rules: Share the recorded carrier, shipment status, latest available scan, and promised date. Describe promised_by as the recorded estimate, not a guaranteed arrival. If the order number is missing or several owned orders could match, ask which order the customer means and use awaiting_customer. General shipping questions do not require an order number. For a status-only request, a supported reply with an outbox receipt can resolve the ticket. Refer late, lost, and delivered-but-not-received cases to POL-SHIP-03. Do not claim to contact the carrier, change a shipment, or open a trace. None of those operations exists in the approved tool set.
Exceptions: An order belonging to another customer follows POL-SEC-02. An unknown ticket ID stops the run under the tool contract. Conflicting shipment facts require Delivery staff review; never fill a missing scan or date with an estimate.

passages.title: Cancellation and payment reversal requests
passages.text:
POL-ORD-01 v1.1: Cancellation and payment reversal requests
Conditions: Read the latest owned order.status and shipment record. An order with status processing and no shipment record can be cancelled with cancel_order; no staff approval is needed. cancel_order checks ownership and status itself and refuses shipped orders. It cannot intercept a shipment.
Rules: For an owned unshipped order, call cancel_order with the order ID. After a successful receipt, tell the customer the order is cancelled and the payment is reversed to the original payment method, quoting the receipt ID. The ticket can then be resolved. For a shipped order, explain that the agent cannot stop the shipment and that a delivered eligible item may use the 30-day return process under POL-RET-01. Escalate the cancellation or interception request to Billing staff. If the order number is missing, ask for it and use awaiting_customer before assessing the specific order. General cancellation guidance does not require an order number. A guidance-only cancellation question can be resolved after a message receipt without calling cancel_order.
Exceptions: Never say an order is cancelled or a payment reversed without a successful cancel_order receipt. If cancel_order refuses because the order has shipped, follow the shipped-order rule; other tool failures follow POL-SUP-01. Sorry to hear your Roomba is dropping Wi-Fi. I can help troubleshoot. Here’s a quick checklist to try:
- Power cycle the Roomba (turn off, unplug, wait 30 seconds, then power back on).
- Reconnect to your Wi‑Fi network and ensure the router is functioning normally.
- If possible, connect the Roomba to a different 2.4 GHz Wi‑Fi network to see if the issue persists.
- Check for any firmware updates for the Roomba in the app and install if available.

Your order O-60099 was delivered (carrier USPS, delivered 2026-08-15). If the connectivity problem continues after these steps, tell me which steps you’ve tried and any error messages you see, and I’ll assist with the next options.

Note: I’m referencing the delivered status of your order for context, per our shipment records.
unresolved_requirements: awaiting_customer to provide details of the issue and outcomes of the basic troubleshooting steps
